 Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization,
 and Ices Explorer ("SPHEREx") is a NASA/JPL mission launched to Earth orbit
 March 12 @ 03:10 UTC from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E), Vandenberg
 Space Force Base, via a Falcon 9.
 
 There will then be a 30-day checkout phase to prepare for operations.
 
 BACKGROUND:
  During its nominally 25-month mission, it will use a single instrument
  (spectrophotometer) with a single observing mode and no moving parts to map
  the entire sky every 6 months (four times during the two year mission), in
  102 different color bands, with much greater color resolution than prior
  all-sky maps.
 
  From an Earth-polar 98-minute orbit ~650 km above the terminator line
  (thereby keeping pointing at least 91 degrees away from the Sun), SPHEREx
  will collect data on more than 450 million galaxies along with more than
  100 million stars in the Milky Way in order to characterize the origin
  of the universe.
 
 PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS:
  Dimensions  : 2.6 m tall, 3.2 m wide and deep
  solar panels: 2.67 x 1.02 m, produce 750 Watts
  Total mass  : 502 kg
  Detectors passively cooled to -350 deg. F (-210 C)
  Three cone-shaped photon shields protect from ambient heat
 
 SCIENCE INSTRUMENT:
  Spectrophotometer has three mirrors (effective diameter, 20 cm)
   11 x 3.5 degree field of view
   Six linear variable filters image each section of the sky in
    102 wavelengths of near-infrared
